• Influenza is a viral infection that attacks the respiratory system.
 
• The common cold is an upper respiratory tract infection caused by many different viruses.
 
• **Rhinoviruses **were shown to be major causative agents in mild upper respiratory illness (the common cold).
 
 
 
• Symptoms of influenza can include:
 
 
• Sudden onset of high fever.
 
• Headache, muscle aches and joint pain
 
• Cough (usually dry)
 
• Chills
 
• Sore throat
 
• Nasal congestion and runny nose
 
• Fatigue
 
• Stomach symptoms such as nausea, vomiting or diarrhea may occur but are more common in children than adults.
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cholera, Leprosy, Tuberculosis, Plague, Syphilis and Anthrax** are the few diseases caused by** bacteria.**
 
• **Aspergillosis, Blastomycosis, Candidiasis **are the few infections caused by** Fungi.**
 
• **Malaria, Leishmaniasis, Toxoplasmosis **are the few diseases caused by **Protozoa.**

questions.question: Which of the following crops is an example of Kharif Crops ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cotton**__.

__
 
• Cotton is a Kharif crop. It requires **6 to 8 months to mature.**
 
• Cotton is a water-thirsty crop and around** 6% of the water **for irrigation in is used for its cultivation. 
 
• It grows in the major parts of the country viz. **Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra and parts of Andhra Pradesh & Karnataka.**
 
• The irrigated crop is sown from March-May and the rain fed crop in June-July with the commencement of the monsoon.

 
• **Kharif Season**:

 
 
• **Kharif crops** also are known as monsoon crops as they are cultivated in the monsoon season.
 
• These crops are sown at the beginning of the rainy season.
 
• Rice, maize, bajra, ragi, sorghum, soybean, groundnut, **cotton**__, etc. are all Kharif types of crops.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Zaid Season**:

 
 
• It is a short season between Kharif and Rabi season.
 
• The crops grown during this season are known as Zaid crops.
 
• Pumpkin, cucumber, watermelon, bitter gourd, etc. are all zaid types of crops. 
 
 
 
• **Rabi Season**:
 
 
• These are the crops that are sown at the end of the monsoon season or at the beginning of the winter season.
 
• These crops also are known as winter crops.
 
• **Wheat**, Mustard, Peas, Pulses, Barley, etc. are all Rabi types of crops.

questions.question: The process of impeachment of the President of India can be initiated in:

options.text: Rajya Sabha but not in Lok Sabha
Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha or any state legislative assembly
Lok Sabha but not in Rajya Sabha

questions.solution:
The correct answer is**__ either house of the parliament.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The President may be removed from office before the completion of this term through impeachment for violating the Constitution of India by the Parliament of India.
 
• The process of impeachment of the President of India can be initiated in either house of the parliament and such resolution has to be passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the House.
 
• Article 61 of the Indian Constitution provides the Procedure for impeachment of the President Of India.
 
• President is elected for a term of five years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Qualifications of the President are**:

 
 
• He should be an Indian Citizen
 
• His age should be a minimum of 35 years
 
• He should qualify the conditions to be elected as a member of the Lok Sabha
 
• He should not hold any office of profit under the central government, state government, or any public authority.
 
 
 
• The President is elected indirectly by members of an electoral college consisting of:
 
 
• the elected members of both the Houses of Parliament;
 
• the elected members of the legislative assemblies of the states;
 
• the elected members of the legislative assemblies of the Union Territories of Delhi and Puducherry.
 
 
 
• The election is held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
